sections.content: Great Falls, Montana does not make headlines the way Bozeman or Missoula do, and that is exactly why smart investors are paying attention. Tucked along the Missouri River in Cascade County, this mid-sized city of roughly 60,000 people offers something rare in today's market: affordability. Median home prices sit well below the national average, rental demand is consistent, and competition from other investors is far lower than in Montana's trendier markets. Whether you are a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started, you will want to read our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in — but this article will give you a detailed picture of what makes Great Falls worth your time and capital.
Great Falls MT Real Estate Market Overview

Great Falls is the third-largest city in Montana, sitting at the crossroads of agriculture, military, and light industry. Malmstrom Air Force Base is one of the city's largest employers, providing a reliable base of renters who rotate in and out on two-to-four-year tours of duty. This military presence creates consistent rental demand that cushions investors against market downturns. The local economy also draws from healthcare, retail, and government employment, giving it a diversified foundation that keeps vacancy rates manageable even when other parts of the country are struggling.

As of mid-2024, the median home price in Great Falls hovers around $230,000 to $250,000. That is a significant jump from just a few years ago — prices have risen roughly 25 to 30 percent since 2020 — but the market still looks affordable compared to national medians above $400,000. Days on market average between 30 and 50 days for move-in-ready homes, though distressed properties can sit longer, creating opportunity for investors willing to negotiate. Explore the full data snapshot on the [Great Falls MT market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/great-falls-mt) to see current deal activity in the area.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Great Falls
Neighborhoods With the Strongest Investor Potential

items: South Great Falls: Working-class neighborhood with high renter concentration and homes priced between $130,000 and $190,000. Ideal for buy-and-hold investors seeking strong cash flow at low entry costs.
Riverview / North Side: Older housing stock from the 1940s–1970s with high fix-and-flip potential. ARVs often land between $200,000 and $280,000 depending on finishes and lot size.

Neighborhood Near Malmstrom AFB: Military tenants make this zone one of the most dependable rental corridors in the city. Single-family homes rent for $1,100 to $1,500 per month, with strong lease renewal rates.
Downtown Core and Adjacent Streets: Increasing interest in commercial-to-residential conversions and small multi-family units. Zoning changes have opened up new possibilities for creative investors.
West Bank / Black Eagle: Undervalued pockets with distressed properties and motivated sellers, especially among aging homeowners looking to downsize or exit.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Drive or virtually tour zip codes 59401 and 59405 first. These two zip codes contain the highest concentration of distressed listings, pre-foreclosures, and absentee-owned properties in Great Falls. Pull a list, skip trace it, and start your outreach there before going anywhere else.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Great Falls MT
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling works well in Great Falls because the market has a steady supply of motivated sellers: estate sales, tax-delinquent properties, code-violation homes, and military families who need to sell quickly due to orders. Assignment fees in this market typically range from $5,000 to $20,000 depending on the deal, with experienced wholesalers closing 2 to 4 deals per month once their pipeline is built. If you are new to the strategy, start with our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide to understand the mechanics before approaching sellers. The key is finding homes at 60 to 70 cents on the dollar relative to ARV and leaving enough room for your end buyer to profit.
Fix-and-Flip Opportunities

The fix-and-flip model is viable in Great Falls, but investors need to run their numbers carefully. Labor costs in Montana are moderate, but materials and contractor availability can be tighter than in major metros. A typical flip in the Riverview corridor might involve purchasing a home for $110,000, spending $55,000 on renovations, and selling for $220,000 — a gross profit of roughly $55,000 before holding costs, financing, and closing fees. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly model your after-repair value before committing to a purchase. Successful flippers in this market focus on cosmetic rehabs rather than full gut jobs to keep timelines under 90 days.
Rental Properties and Buy-and-Hold

The buy-and-hold strategy may offer the most reliable returns in Great Falls right now. Single-family rentals near Malmstrom AFB generate gross rents of $1,100 to $1,600 per month, and small multi-family properties — duplexes and triplexes — are available in the $200,000 to $320,000 range. With the right financing, investors can achieve gross rent multipliers under 10 and cap rates between 6 and 9 percent, which is competitive by current national standards. Vacancy rates in the city tend to run between 5 and 8 percent, lower than many comparable markets.

"The best real estate markets aren't always the hottest ones. They're the ones where demand is stable, inventory is available, and the competition hasn't caught up yet. Great Falls fits that description exactly right now."
Local Market Trends Investors Should Know

Several trends are shaping the Great Falls market heading into 2025. First, inventory remains tight but is slowly increasing as higher interest rates have kept some buyers on the sidelines and motivated sellers to list. Second, the rental market remains undersupplied, particularly for three-bedroom homes near the base, which means landlords have pricing power. Third, remote-work migration into Montana continues, though Great Falls draws more from the practical relocation crowd — people seeking affordable living — rather than the luxury buyers gravitating toward Bozeman. This keeps price growth moderate and sustainable rather than speculative. Finally, the city has invested in downtown revitalization, which is slowly driving appreciation in adjacent neighborhoods.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Great Falls

The best real estate deals in Great Falls MT are rarely listed on Zillow. Off-market properties — those found through direct mail, cold calling, driving for dollars, and probate leads — are where the real margins are. Because the local investor community is smaller than in cities like Billings or Missoula, you face less competition on every deal you source. Our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) walks you through exactly how to build a lead pipeline in any market, including smaller cities like Great Falls. Focus on absentee owners, tax-delinquent lists pulled from Cascade County, and properties with code violations logged with the city building department.

Pro Tip: Contact the Cascade County Treasurer's office to request the current tax delinquency list. Properties with two or more years of unpaid taxes are your highest-priority leads — these owners are often motivated to sell quickly and may accept below-market offers.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Looking at Great Falls MT

items: Build a local team first: You need a reliable real estate agent who works with investors, a contractor who understands Montana building codes, and a property manager familiar with military tenant needs.
Understand the seasonal market: Montana winters affect construction timelines and listing activity. Plan your acquisitions for spring through early fall to avoid renovation delays.

Use virtual tools to underwrite deals: Run comps and analyze potential returns using AIWholesail's free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) before booking a flight.
Factor in insurance costs: Montana properties face hail, wind, and winter weather claims. Get insurance quotes before closing — premiums can be higher than investors from warmer states expect.

Study the military housing allowance (BAH): Malmstrom personnel receive BAH rates that directly influence what military tenants can afford to pay. Align your rent pricing to BAH rates for faster leasing.
Verify zoning before purchasing multi-family properties: Cascade County zoning rules can limit conversions. Always confirm permitted uses with the county planning department.
Learn to [analyze real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) using a consistent framework so you can evaluate any property quickly, even from out of state.

sections.content: Great Falls rewards patient, data-driven investors who do their homework. The market lacks the glamour of resort towns, but it offers something more valuable: consistent demand, affordable prices, and room for margin at every stage of the deal cycle. Whether you are wholesaling, flipping, or building a rental portfolio, the fundamentals here are solid — and the competition has not caught up yet.
